hwe_bench.problem_statement: Observed behavior: in XiangShan's Control and Status Register (CSR) unit, writing `mstatus` with the `XS` bits set changes the read-only extension-status state (`xstatus.xs`), so a subsequent `mstatus` read can report non-zero `XS` and set `SD`. A write to `satp` can also preserve `PPN` bits above the implementation's supported physical-address width. Expected behavior: software writes must not modify the read-only `XS` field, so `mstatus` readback should leave `XS` unchanged and should not set `SD` because of that write. `satp.ppn` should be limited to the implemented physical-page-number width and discard unsupported high bits on readback. Affected function: CSR read/write handling for `mstatus`/`xstatus` and `satp` in XiangShan. Trigger condition: the bug appears when software writes `mstatus` with `XS` bits set, or writes `satp` with high `PPN` bits set on configurations whose physical address width is narrower than the architectural `satp.ppn` field.

reduction.limitations: Reauthored interface and minimal environment isolate one contract; this does not reproduce upstream integration, performance, or full regression behavior.
reduction.preserved_contract: Preserve old_mstatus_i[5:4] across writes and accept all other mstatus bits. Keep only satp_ppn_i[11:0], forcing its upper four output bits to zero.
reduction.preserved_mechanism: CSR writes could modify a read-only status field and preserve page-number bits above the implementation's physical-address width.

upstream.title: csr: add write mask to satp.ppn & xstatus.xs
